Osmosis.subject: Plant Physiology & Nutrition
Osmosis.question: The _____ was Movement of molecules to lower concentration.
Osmosis.fact: Osmosis (, US also ) is the spontaneous net movement of solvent molecules through a selectively permeable membrane from a region of high water potential (region of lower solute concentration) to a region of low water potential (region of higher solute concentration), in the direction that tends to equalize the solute concentrations on the two sides. Osmosis can be made to do work.

Oxidative stress.question: The _____ was Free radical toxicity.
Oxidative stress.fact: Oxidative stress reflects an imbalance between the systemic manifestation of reactive oxygen species and a biological system's ability to readily detoxify the reactive intermediates or to repair the resulting damage. Oxidative stress from oxidative metabolism causes base damage, as well as strand breaks in DNA.

Root hair.fact: Root hairs or absorbent hairs, are outgrowths of epidermal cells, specialized cells at the tip of a plant root. Root hair cells improve plant water absorption by increasing root surface area to volume ratio which allows the root hair cell to take in more water.

Root pressure.fact: Root pressure is the transverse osmotic pressure within the cells of a root system that causes sap to rise through a plant stem to the leaves.
